title: EU logo (European Commission)
summary: The European Commission logo builds itself up: stripes fly in, the flag unfolds, twelve stars pop in.
description: The Berlaymont logo of the European Commission as an interactive Rive animation. On load the grey stripes fly in from the sides, the blue flag unfolds and the twelve stars pop in one by one, clockwise. A highlight makes the flag grow, light up and jump. Click or tap the logo to play the highlight; the durations, the size and the jump height are adjustable.

controls.name: entree
controls.label: Play entrance
controls.description: Replays the entrance animation. It also plays once by itself when the file loads.

controls.name: highlight
controls.label: Play highlight
controls.description: A short attention move: the flag grows, lights up and jumps, in front of the stripes.

controls.name: entreeDuur
controls.label: Entrance duration
controls.description: Length of the entrance in seconds. The file snaps to the nearest of 0.7, 0.9, 1.1, 1.4, 1.7, 2.1, 2.6, 3.2 or 4.

controls.name: highlightDuur
controls.label: Highlight duration
controls.description: Length of the highlight in seconds. Snaps to the nearest of 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1.1, 1.5, 2 or 2.7.

controls.name: highlightGrootte
controls.label: Highlight size
controls.description: How much it grows during the highlight, in percent (100 = no growth). Stepless.

controls.name: highlightHoogte
controls.label: Highlight jump
controls.description: How far it jumps up during the highlight, in artboard pixels (0 = no jump). Stepless.

controls.name: aangeraakt
controls.label: Touched
controls.description: Set by the file's own click listener, so clicking or tapping the logo plays the highlight. Leave it alone.

notes: Plays its entrance by itself on load; fire `entree` to replay it.
Clicking or tapping the logo plays the highlight; that listener is built into the file.
To draw attention now and then, fire `highlight` at random intervals (for example every 1 to 5 minutes) and skip it while the tab is hidden.
The stripes are light grey, so on white they are subtle; on a dark background they stand out more.
author: Stijlbreuk
